record.context_brief: General Ramsey analogue for infinite structures
record.original_question: For which infinite structures S does the following Ramsey-type boundedness phenomenon hold: for every finite substructure A of S, there is a positive integer T such that whenever all copies of A inside S are colored with finitely many colors, one can find a subcopy S' of S in which the copies of A use at most T colors?

evidence.quote: Question 1.3. For which infinite structures S is there a Ramsey-analogue in the following sense: Let A be a finite substructure of S. Is there a positive integer T such that for any coloring of the copies of A into finitely many colors, there is a subcopy S′ of S in which there are no more than T many colors for the copies of A?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let S be a countably infinite relational (or more generally first-order) structure. For a finite substructure A of S, write $\binom{S}{A}$ for the set of isomorphic copies of A inside S. Say that S has the bounded-Ramsey property (finite big Ramsey degrees) if for every finite substructure A of S there exists a positive integer T = T(A, S) such that for every finite coloring $c : \binom{S}{A} \to \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (with k arbitrary finite) there exists an isomorphic copy $S' \subseteq S$ of S such that the restriction of c to $\binom{S'}{A}$ takes at most T distinct values.

Characterize the infinite structures S for which the bounded-Ramsey property holds. That is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on S guaranteeing that, for every finite substructure A of S, such a uniform bound T exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification of infinite structures with finite big Ramsey degrees remains an active open program. Recent work (e.g., Balko–Chodounský–Dobrinen–Hubička–Konečný–Vena–Zucker, 2023–2024) establishes finite big Ramsey degrees for new classes such as unrestricted relational structures in infinite languages and provides a survey of big Ramsey structures, but a full characterization of which infinite structures admit finite big Ramsey degrees is explicitly listed as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: A survey on big Ramsey structures
status_evidence.snippet: In all known examples of infinite structures with finite big Ramsey degrees... the big Ramsey degrees of many classes of structures with finite small Ramsey degrees are still not well understood.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of infinite structures with finite big Ramsey degrees is still an active open area as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: Big Ramsey Degrees and Infinite Languages
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes finite big Ramsey degrees for unrestricted relational structures with finitely many relations of each arity > 1.
status_evidence.claim: New cases continue to be settled, but the general question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of current trends and open problems in Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures.
status_evidence.claim: The general bounded-Ramsey question is listed among open problems.
